sentence: HLA-A *31:01 is associated with increased risk of hypersensitivity (particularly hypersensitivity syndrome [HSS], and also maculopapular exanthema) when treated with carbamazepine in children from ethnically diverse Canadian pediatric hospitals as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: The study of pediatric CPNDS participants replicated the HLA-A*31:01 risk association (dominant model, Fisher’s exact test), noted a stronger signal for HSS versus MPE, and did not detect an association with SJS/TEN in this cohort (limited SJS/TEN cases).
citations: HLA-A*31:01 was significantly associated with CBZ-HSS (odds ratio (OR): 26.4, p=0.0025) and maculopapular exanthems (OR: 8.6, p=0.0037), but not with CBZ-SJS.

Three of six patients (50%) with CBZ-HSS carried HLA-A*31:01, whereas only three (3.3%) of the 91 CBZ-tolerant controls carried the allele, resulting in a very strong association with CBZ-HSS (OR: 26.4; P=0.0025; [Table 2]).
A significant association was also observed with CBZ-induced MPE, with six of 26 (23.1%) CBZ-MPE cases carrying HLA-A*31:01 (OR: 8.6; P=0.0037; [Table 2]).

In contrast to the strong associations with HSS and MPE, no HLA-A*31:01 or rs1061235T carriers were detected among the nine patients with CBZ-induced SJS/TEN, and no significant association with CBZ-SJS/TEN was observed (OR: 1.33; P=1.00; [Table 2]).

sentence: HLA-B *15:02 is associated with increased risk of severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SJS/TEN) when treated with carbamazepine in children in Canada, particularly those of Asian origin, as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: In the pediatric CPNDS cohort, all CBZ-SJS/TEN cases with Asian ancestry carried HLA-B*15:02, confirming a well-established association; analyses used Fisher’s exact test under a dominant model.
citations: Conversely, HLA-B*15:02 was associated with CBZ-SJS (OR: 38.6, p=0.002), but not HSS and maculopapular exanthems.
On the other hand, three of the nine patients with CBZ-SJS/TEN were carriers of HLA-B*15:02, resulting in a significant association of HLA-B*15:02 with CBZ-SJS/TEN (OR: 38.6; P=0.002; [Table 2]).
All three HLA-B*15:02-positive patients with CBZ-SJS/TEN were of Asian origin and included the patient with concurrent Mycoplasma infection.
None of the patients with CBZ-HSS or MPE carried HLA-B*15:02 ([Table 2]).

In contrast, the observed association of HLA-B*15:02 with CBZ-SJS/TEN is in full agreement with previous findings ([23]–[25], [40]–[42]) with HLA-B*15:02 being observed in all children with CBZ-SJS/TEN who reported Asian origins.

sentence: Allele T of rs1061235 is associated with increased risk of carbamazepine-induced hypersensitivity in children from ethnically diverse Canadian pediatric hospitals, including in those not carrying HLA-A*31:01, as compared to non-T carriers.
explanation: The study genotyped rs1061235 (a proxy for HLA-A*31:01 in Europeans) and observed T-allele overrepresentation among hypersensitivity cases, though the authors cautioned it is not an optimal surrogate in multiethnic populations.
citations: A highly significant association with CBZ-HSS and MPE was also observed for the HLA-A*31:01 proxy SNP rs1061235 with 14 (33%) CBZ hypersensitivity cases and only six (6.6%) control patients carrying the T allele (combined OR: 9.45; P=2.6×10^−5; [Table 2]).

Interestingly, rs1061235 was also overrepresented in hypersensitivity cases after excluding HLA-A*31:01-positive children (OR: 5.83; P=0.033; [Supplementary Table 1]), resulting in very similar effect sizes of the associations with HSS and MPE for HLA-A*31:01 and rs1061235.

Interestingly, a majority of patients with West or South Asian origin who carried rs1061235T did not carry HLA-A*31:01, suggesting that rs1061235 alone is not an optimal proxy SNP in some populations.
Of importance, we showed that the proxy SNP rs1061235 is not an optimal surrogate marker for HLA-A*31:01 in ancestrally diverse populations.
